question: A 28-year-old man has an intra-abdominal swelling that has been present since childhood, is non-tender, soft, fluctuant, and transilluminates brilliantly. CT confirms a thin-walled cystic structure arising from the mesentery with no solid components. The most appropriate management is:

answers.text: IV antibiotics and image-guided drainage — the standard treatment for intra-abdominal collections

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Antibiotics + drainage is appropriate for an intra-abdominal abscess (which would be tender with fever). A mesenteric cyst is sterile and congenital; drainage alone risks recurrence without excision.

answers.text: Complete surgical excision of the cyst — the treatment of choice for a mesenteric cyst

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Mesenteric cysts are benign congenital lymphatic malformations that require complete surgical excision to prevent recurrence. They are not drained (incomplete treatment) nor biopsied-only.

answers.text: Core needle biopsy followed by chemotherapy — appropriate for a retroperitoneal sarcoma

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Retroperitoneal sarcomas are solid, not brilliantly transilluminant thin-walled cysts. The classic transillumination + childhood onset + mesenteric origin clinch a mesenteric cyst.

overallFeedback.feedback: The key discriminator is transillumination: true mesenteric cysts transilluminate brilliantly and require complete excision; abscesses are hot and tender; sarcomas are solid masses.
Well done. Transillumination + mesenteric origin = mesenteric cyst → complete surgical excision.
